title: JD Vance delivers speech at the 61st Munich Security Conference
body:
On 14 February 2025, US Vice President JD Vance addressed the 61st Munich Security Conference at the Hotel Bayerischer Hof in Munich, Germany. His speech took place two days after President Donald Trump's telephone call with Russian President Vladimir Putin, which had appeared to exclude Ukraine and Europe from the start of negotiations.

Vance argued that the principal threat to Europe came from within, through democratic backsliding, censorship and the exclusion of populist voices, rather than from Russia or China. He criticised the annulment of Romania's 2024 presidential election over alleged foreign interference, and he criticised United Kingdom and Scottish laws as well as a Swedish conviction for a Quran burning. He described mass immigration as Europe's most significant problem. He said US support would depend on European governments upholding free speech and political legitimacy, and that European governments were "running in fear of their own voters." He also urged Europe to raise its defence spending.

Vance mentioned Ukraine only briefly, referring to a possible "reasonable settlement." Attendees had hoped for more detail on peace negotiations.

German Defence Minister Boris Pistorius said Vance's comparison of parts of Europe to authoritarian regimes was "not acceptable." EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said she felt the United States was "trying to pick a fight with us." Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said she agreed with Vance's message. Trump praised the speech.
